localChanges: New Game → Rules → Enhanced rules has a new rule, on to start with: the advances a civilization starts with count toward its research costs, its power ranking and its chance of pollution, as they always have. Switch it off to play as the original Civilization does, where only the advances gained once the game is under way count (closes #973).

log: feat: respawn for a rule set, and a player joining with rules held off (#2)

respawn adds the advances a returning civilization inherits as starting advances (core-science's addAdvance(Advance, { starting: true })), not as advances gained in play, so a ruleset that counts only those, as Civ1's tech_count does, counts none of them.

addStartingAdvances adds its advances as starting advances (core-science's PlayerResearch#startingAdvances()), and lib/count's gainedInPlay counts the advances a player knows less those, for a ruleset's AdvanceCount rule.
The pollution roll's advances are those counted by the game's AdvanceCount rules, plus 1, as for the research cost: with civ1-science's rule, only those gained in play.

A new set, civ1-enhanced:starting-advances-count (STARTING_ADVANCES_COUNT), on to start with, counts every advance a player knows, those it started with too, for its research costs, power ranking and chance of pollution, as the game always has. It takes the place of civ1-science's v474.05 count of only those gained in play.
chore: require base-game-end 0.1.2, whose respawn marks inherited advances as starting ones (civ-clone/web-renderer#973) (#7)
The ranking score's advances term is the advances counted by the game's AdvanceCount rules, plus 1: v474.05's tech_count, with civ1-science's rule counting only those gained in play.

A new AdvanceCount rule, civ1-science:research/advance-count/gained-in-play (ADVANCE_COUNT_RULE), counts the advances a player knows less those it started with. The research cost, its human floor and its catch-up all count by the game's AdvanceCount rules, and without the game's rules by the advances gained in play.

PlayerResearch keeps the advances a player started with apart from those gained in play: addAdvance(Advance, { starting: true }) marks one, startingAdvances() lists them, and a game saved before they were kept reads as having none.

Rules/AdvanceCount says how many advances a player is counted as knowing, for the rules that weigh it (a research cost, a ranking); advanceCount() asks it and counts every advance known when no rule answers.
